head_commit.message:
fix: make clicking an OS notification open the app, on the right screen (#949)

* fix: make clicking an os notification open the app, on the right screen

Reported twice: clicking a Windows notification does nothing, and there was no
way to jump from a notification to the thing it was about.

Both had one cause. `tauri-plugin-notification`'s desktop `show()` is
notify-rust fire-and-forget, and the `onAction` JS helper its docs point at for
clicks resolves to `plugin:notification|register_listener` — a command the
plugin registers ONLY on mobile (its desktop invoke_handler is exactly notify,
request_permission, is_permission_granted). So the renderer's subscription
failed with "Command not found" on every desktop startup and no banner click
ever reached the app. `notifications_clicked` — which already does the right
thing — had no caller other than the tray.

Show the banner natively instead, per platform, since only Windows is
callback-based:

- Windows: tauri-winrt-notification's on_activated, non-blocking.
- macOS/Linux: notify-rust's wait_for_action BLOCKS, so it runs on
  spawn_blocking. Linux additionally needs a declared `default` action for a
  body click to be delivered at all.

Both crates were already in the tree transitively; they are pinned to the
locked versions so there is no duplicate copy.

Routing: the click now carries the clicked notification's OWN route, so
"Autopilot X found 3 jobs" opens THAT autopilot rather than a list to search.
Every notification source already attached a route (autopilot -> /autopilot with
its id) and the bell already followed it — only the OS banner didn't. Validated
through the same resolveNotificationRoute the bell uses, so an unknown backend
route falls back instead of breaking navigation. A tray click sends no route and
still just opens the inbox.

The dead renderer seam (onOsBannerClick) is removed, which also silences the
startup console error it produced.

Known limit, all platforms: the callback lives in this process, so it fires only
while the app runs. A click after the app exits needs a COM activator on Windows
and is out of scope.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: bound banner listeners and close the windows ci gap

Four review findings, all real.

The macOS/Linux path parks a blocking thread in wait_for_action until the user
clicks or the banner closes — and a notification nobody touches (sitting in
macOS Notification Center) parks it indefinitely. OsBanner::Always sources like
autopilot can emit a burst, so a run of ignored notifications would hold
blocking workers permanently and starve every other spawn_blocking caller.

Bounded to 8 concurrent listeners via an RAII slot (released on Drop, so a panic
inside the wait cannot leak the budget). Over budget the banner is still
DELIVERED — on Linux show() already sent it, and macOS's handle Drop sends it —
it just has no click handler. Losing one banner's click beats starving the pool.
The async alternative was checked and rejected: wait_for_action_async exists
only on Linux, and behind a feature that swaps the dbus backend.

Windows had the same CI hole this branch opened the macOS job for: no PR job
compiles cfg(windows), so the notification code that actually fixes the reported
bug was built only on the dev machine. Added the counterpart.

Also corrected the macOS job's own comment, which overstated the gap:
cfg(not(windows)) IS compiled by the ubuntu jobs — only platform-exclusive
predicates were uncovered.

And the route tests now use the shared NotificationOpen type instead of local
structural aliases; they exist to guard that contract, so a local shape could
not detect drift in it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix: the macOS bug report — docx sizes, blocked pdf downloads, empty generations, and logs you can actually read (#948)

* fix: write docx font sizes in half-points, not twentieths of a point

A user's exported CV came out as 132 pages of enormous text. `w:sz` is in
half-points, but every font size went through `pt_to_dxa` (pt × 20 — the
correct unit for spacing, indentation and page geometry, not type). A 10.5pt
body font was written as `w:sz val="210"`, i.e. 105pt. Every DOCX export, on
every platform, since the renderer was written.

24 call sites now route through `pt_to_half_points` (pt × 2, rounded — odd
half-point sizes like 10.5 → 21 are representable and were previously
truncated). The genuine dxa uses — line spacing, section spacing, indents —
are unchanged, and border widths never went through the helper at all.

No test asserted `w:sz` anywhere, which is how a 10× error survived: the
DOCX suite covered page size, fonts and colours only. There are now exact
size assertions for both writers plus a ceiling guard that fails if any run
exceeds 50pt, which catches this whole class rather than these constants.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: stop false-blocking cover-letter pdfs and make export diagnosable

A user could not download their PDF while the same document exported to
DOCX fine. `header_url_mismatch` is the only critical check gated to PDF
only, which is what made the asymmetry findable at all.

Its résumé arm was narrowed to the topmost N links after two prior
false-block regressions. The cover-letter arm still checked every link in
the top 144pt band unconditionally, justified by "no body section can
render early into its band" — true of a body section, not of a body link in
the opening paragraph, which `tokenize_rich` will happily turn into a real
PDF annotation. With company research on, a model echoing a researched URL
in its first sentence lands there. And a cover letter is never two-column,
so `can_linearize` is false: the user got a hard block with no remediation
offered. Now narrowed the same way, verified by reverting the file and
watching the new test fail on old code with the incident's exact shape.

The bundle that reported this had no export log lines at all — the command
computed a full report with per-issue codes and threw all of it away except
a concatenated string. Export now uses the `Span` idiom the rest of the app
already uses, and logs the issue CODES on a block, never the messages,
which can embed a URL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: treat an empty generation as a failure instead of a result

A user's CV and cover letter both came out empty with no error shown, and
regenerating produced real content. `awaitAiStream` has two resolve paths —
the stream's `done` chunk and the job-status poll fallback — and neither
checked for content, so an empty completion was persisted and displayed as
a successful generation.

Both paths now reject on whitespace-only output. Neither caller needed a
change: `handleGenerate` and `runTailor` already persist only on the success
path, so rejecting at the source was enough — the same reasoning as the
import fix in #947.

Also logs job id + provider/model on the empty path, never the content.
That absence is why the reporter's bundle showed nothing.

What produced an empty stream in the first place is still unknown; this
only stops it being silent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: stop two whole-response eaters and record why a stream produced nothing

The reporter on ollama-cloud/gpt-oss:120b got an empty CV and cover letter
with no error. Two independent causes, both of which delete or discard a
complete response:

`extractPlainText` strips fenced code blocks, so a model that wraps its
ENTIRE answer in one fence had the whole document deleted — verified at
zero length for a bare fence, a language-tagged fence, and a fence with a
trailing newline. This was already found and fixed in `github-projects.ts`,
whose comment names the failure outright; the shared helper every résumé
and cover-letter generation runs through was never touched. Now unwraps
only when the entire trimmed response is one fence, so a genuine mid-answer
snippet is still stripped as before.

`finish()` persisted a zero-content stream as a completed job. A reasoning
model that never reaches its final channel leaves `answer` empty while the
stream itself succeeded, and every consumer read that as success. It now
errors the same way a transport failure does, which routes the extension
bridge and CLI-agent paths correctly without touching either.

`finish_reason` was never parsed, so "ran out of budget mid-reasoning" was
indistinguishable from a clean empty stream — that ambiguity is why this
needed two investigations. It is now parsed and reported distinctly.

Also prices gpt-oss: with no matching RATES row it fell through to the
3.00/15.00 default, billing a cheap open-weights model at Claude Sonnet
rates. Ollama Cloud publishes no per-token figure, so the rows use
OpenRouter's live published rate for the same model.

Stream start and end now log provider, model, answer/thinking lengths,
finish reason and usage — ids, counts and enum values only, never content.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: make the logs actually reach the file a user can send

Two reasons the reporter's diagnostics bundle was nearly empty, neither of
which was a missing log call.

The global level filter is Warn and only `cover_letter::research` was raised
to Info — which is exactly why research briefs were the sole app content in
their bundle. Every `Span` line in the app logs under one target, so raising
`observability` covers ai, scrape, apply, autopilot, pipeline and export at
once, plus the stream module for its own two lines. A regression test pins
the module path against the filter target, so moving the file can't silently
turn every span dark again.

And no renderer log had ever reached the file at all: `attachConsole` mirrors
Rust logs INTO devtools, the opposite direction, so following that route
would have shipped a bridge that does nothing. The console methods now
forward to the plugin, which captures every existing call site for free. The
capability it needs was already granted.

Renderer generation and export paths now log start/done/failed. They use
warn deliberately — the repo bans `console.info`, and warn is what the
current filter passes, so the two halves need not agree on a level.

End-to-end delivery is NOT verified: the unit tests prove the forwarding
logic against a mock, not that the IPC round-trip lands in the file. That
needs a real run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: stop logging absolute paths into shareable diagnostics bundles

`AGENTS.md` forbids absolute paths, usernames and home dirs anywhere,
logs included. Two sites violated it at warn/error, so they were in
bundles today — and this branch is actively asking users to send bundles.
One arrived over Telegram this week.

`postings` logged the full `interactions.json` path four times; the message
already names the file, so most lines lose the path entirely and the rest
log a file name. `extension_bridge` was harder: six browsers share one
manifest filename in different directories, so a bare name would be
ambiguous — it now takes a caller-supplied label instead of deriving
anything from the path.

Swept the whole tree for the class rather than fixing only what was
reported: 90 `.display()` sites and every log/tracing call. No other
production leaks. `std::io::Error` from `fs` does not embed the path in its
Display, and the diagnostics-bundle builder and Sentry already run through
a shared redaction gate — both confirmed rather than assumed.

New architecture rule R15 fails on `.display()` inside a log or tracing
macro, with an empty allowlist. It deliberately ignores `.display()`
elsewhere: a path in an error the user reads about their own file is

fix: the macOS bug report — docx sizes, blocked pdf downloads, empty generations, and logs you can actually read (#948)

* fix: write docx font sizes in half-points, not twentieths of a point

A user's exported CV came out as 132 pages of enormous text. `w:sz` is in
half-points, but every font size went through `pt_to_dxa` (pt × 20 — the
correct unit for spacing, indentation and page geometry, not type). A 10.5pt
body font was written as `w:sz val="210"`, i.e. 105pt. Every DOCX export, on
every platform, since the renderer was written.

24 call sites now route through `pt_to_half_points` (pt × 2, rounded — odd
half-point sizes like 10.5 → 21 are representable and were previously
truncated). The genuine dxa uses — line spacing, section spacing, indents —
are unchanged, and border widths never went through the helper at all.

No test asserted `w:sz` anywhere, which is how a 10× error survived: the
DOCX suite covered page size, fonts and colours only. There are now exact
size assertions for both writers plus a ceiling guard that fails if any run
exceeds 50pt, which catches this whole class rather than these constants.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: stop false-blocking cover-letter pdfs and make export diagnosable

A user could not download their PDF while the same document exported to
DOCX fine. `header_url_mismatch` is the only critical check gated to PDF
only, which is what made the asymmetry findable at all.

Its résumé arm was narrowed to the topmost N links after two prior
false-block regressions. The cover-letter arm still checked every link in
the top 144pt band unconditionally, justified by "no body section can
render early into its band" — true of a body section, not of a body link in
the opening paragraph, which `tokenize_rich` will happily turn into a real
PDF annotation. With company research on, a model echoing a researched URL
in its first sentence lands there. And a cover letter is never two-column,
so `can_linearize` is false: the user got a hard block with no remediation
offered. Now narrowed the same way, verified by reverting the file and
watching the new test fail on old code with the incident's exact shape.

The bundle that reported this had no export log lines at all — the command
computed a full report with per-issue codes and threw all of it away except
a concatenated string. Export now uses the `Span` idiom the rest of the app
already uses, and logs the issue CODES on a block, never the messages,
which can embed a URL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: treat an empty generation as a failure instead of a result

A user's CV and cover letter both came out empty with no error shown, and
regenerating produced real content. `awaitAiStream` has two resolve paths —
the stream's `done` chunk and the job-status poll fallback — and neither
checked for content, so an empty completion was persisted and displayed as
a successful generation.

Both paths now reject on whitespace-only output. Neither caller needed a
change: `handleGenerate` and `runTailor` already persist only on the success
path, so rejecting at the source was enough — the same reasoning as the
import fix in #947.

Also logs job id + provider/model on the empty path, never the content.
That absence is why the reporter's bundle showed nothing.

What produced an empty stream in the first place is still unknown; this
only stops it being silent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: stop two whole-response eaters and record why a stream produced nothing

The reporter on ollama-cloud/gpt-oss:120b got an empty CV and cover letter
with no error. Two independent causes, both of which delete or discard a
complete response:

`extractPlainText` strips fenced code blocks, so a model that wraps its
ENTIRE answer in one fence had the whole document deleted — verified at
zero length for a bare fence, a language-tagged fence, and a fence with a
trailing newline. This was already found and fixed in `github-projects.ts`,
whose comment names the failure outright; the shared helper every résumé
and cover-letter generation runs through was never touched. Now unwraps
only when the entire trimmed response is one fence, so a genuine mid-answer
snippet is still stripped as before.

`finish()` persisted a zero-content stream as a completed job. A reasoning
model that never reaches its final channel leaves `answer` empty while the
stream itself succeeded, and every consumer read that as success. It now
errors the same way a transport failure does, which routes the extension
bridge and CLI-agent paths correctly without touching either.

`finish_reason` was never parsed, so "ran out of budget mid-reasoning" was
indistinguishable from a clean empty stream — that ambiguity is why this
needed two investigations. It is now parsed and reported distinctly.

Also prices gpt-oss: with no matching RATES row it fell through to the
3.00/15.00 default, billing a cheap open-weights model at Claude Sonnet
rates. Ollama Cloud publishes no per-token figure, so the rows use
OpenRouter's live published rate for the same model.

Stream start and end now log provider, model, answer/thinking lengths,
finish reason and usage — ids, counts and enum values only, never content.

* fix: make the logs actually reach the file a user can send

which was a missing log call.

capability it needs was already granted.

warn deliberately — the repo bans `console.info`, and warn is what the
current filter passes, so the two halves need not agree on a level.

End-to-end delivery is NOT verified: the unit tests prove the forwarding
logic against a mock, not that the IPC round-trip lands in the file. That
needs a real run.

* fix: stop logging absolute paths into shareable diagnostics bundles

rather than passing vacuously.

fix: the macOS bug report — docx sizes, blocked pdf downloads, empty generations, and logs you can actually read (#948)

* fix: write docx font sizes in half-points, not twentieths of a point

A user's exported CV came out as 132 pages of enormous text. `w:sz` is in
half-points, but every font size went through `pt_to_dxa` (pt × 20 — the
correct unit for spacing, indentation and page geometry, not type). A 10.5pt
body font was written as `w:sz val="210"`, i.e. 105pt. Every DOCX export, on
every platform, since the renderer was written.

24 call sites now route through `pt_to_half_points` (pt × 2, rounded — odd
half-point sizes like 10.5 → 21 are representable and were previously
truncated). The genuine dxa uses — line spacing, section spacing, indents —
are unchanged, and border widths never went through the helper at all.

No test asserted `w:sz` anywhere, which is how a 10× error survived: the
DOCX suite covered page size, fonts and colours only. There are now exact
size assertions for both writers plus a ceiling guard that fails if any run
exceeds 50pt, which catches this whole class rather than these constants.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: stop false-blocking cover-letter pdfs and make export diagnosable

A user could not download their PDF while the same document exported to
DOCX fine. `header_url_mismatch` is the only critical check gated to PDF
only, which is what made the asymmetry findable at all.

Its résumé arm was narrowed to the topmost N links after two prior
false-block regressions. The cover-letter arm still checked every link in
the top 144pt band unconditionally, justified by "no body section can
render early into its band" — true of a body section, not of a body link in
the opening paragraph, which `tokenize_rich` will happily turn into a real
PDF annotation. With company research on, a model echoing a researched URL
in its first sentence lands there. And a cover letter is never two-column,
so `can_linearize` is false: the user got a hard block with no remediation
offered. Now narrowed the same way, verified by reverting the file and
watching the new test fail on old code with the incident's exact shape.

The bundle that reported this had no export log lines at all — the command
computed a full report with per-issue codes and threw all of it away except
a concatenated string. Export now uses the `Span` idiom the rest of the app
already uses, and logs the issue CODES on a block, never the messages,
which can embed a URL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: treat an empty generation as a failure instead of a result

A user's CV and cover letter both came out empty with no error shown, and
regenerating produced real content. `awaitAiStream` has two resolve paths —
the stream's `done` chunk and the job-status poll fallback — and neither
checked for content, so an empty completion was persisted and displayed as
a successful generation.

Both paths now reject on whitespace-only output. Neither caller needed a
change: `handleGenerate` and `runTailor` already persist only on the success
path, so rejecting at the source was enough — the same reasoning as the
import fix in #947.

Also logs job id + provider/model on the empty path, never the content.
That absence is why the reporter's bundle showed nothing.

What produced an empty stream in the first place is still unknown; this
only stops it being silent.

* fix: stop two whole-response eaters and record why a stream produced nothing

with no error. Two independent causes, both of which delete or discard a
complete response:

ENTIRE answer in one fence had the whole document deleted — verified at
zero length for a bare fence, a language-tagged fence, and a fence with a
trailing newline. This was already found and fixed in `github-projects.ts`,
whose comment names the failure outright; the shared helper every résumé
and cover-letter generation runs through was never touched. Now unwraps
only when the entire trimmed response is one fence, so a genuine mid-answer
snippet is still stripped as before.

`finish()` persisted a zero-content stream as a completed job. A reasoning
model that never reaches its final channel leaves `answer` empty while the
stream itself succeeded, and every consumer read that as success. It now
errors the same way a transport failure does, which routes the extension
bridge and CLI-agent paths correctly without touching either.

`finish_reason` was never parsed, so "ran out of budget mid-reasoning" was
indistinguishable from a clean empty stream — that ambiguity is why this
needed two investigations. It is now parsed and reported distinctly.

capability it needs was already granted.

current filter passes, so the two halves need not agree on a level.

logic against a mock, not that the IPC round-trip lands in the file. That
needs a real run.

ambiguous — it now takes a caller-supplied label instead of deriving

candidate name, company or content.

trailing newline. This was already found and fixed in `github-projects.ts`,
whose comment names the failure outright; the shared helper every résumé
and cover-letter generation runs through was never touched. Now unwraps
only when the entire trimmed response is one fence, so a genuine mid-answer
snippet is still stripped as before.

`finish()` persisted a zero-content stream as a completed job. A reasoning
model that never reaches its final channel leaves `answer` empty while the
stream itself succeeded, and every consumer read that as success. It now
errors the same way a transport failure does, which routes the extension
bridge and CLI-agent paths correctly without touching either.

`finish_reason` was never parsed, so "ran out of budget mid-reasoning" was
indistinguishable from a clean empty stream — that ambiguity is why this
needed two investigations. It is now parsed and reported distinctly.

Also prices gpt-oss: with no matching RATES row it fell through to the
3.00/15.00 default, billing a cheap open-weights model at Claude Sonnet
rates. Ollama Cloud publishes no per-token figure, so the rows use
OpenRouter's live published rate for the same model.

Stream start and end now log provider, model, answer/thinking lengths,
finish reason and usage — ids, counts and enum values only, never content.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: make the logs actually reach the file a user can send

Two reasons the reporter's diagnostics bundle was nearly empty, neither of
which was a missing log call.

The global level filter is Warn and only `cover_letter::research` was raised
to Info — which is exactly why research briefs were the sole app content in
their bundle. Every `Span` line in the app logs under one target, so raising
`observability` covers ai, scrape, apply, autopilot, pipeline and export at
once, plus the stream module for its own two lines. A regression test pins
the module path against the filter target, so moving the file can't silently
turn every span dark again.

And no renderer log had ever reached the file at all: `attachConsole` mirrors
Rust logs INTO devtools, the opposite direction, so following that route
would have shipped a bridge that does nothing. The console methods now
forward to the plugin, which captures every existing call site for free. The
capability it needs was already granted.

Renderer generation and export paths now log start/done/failed. They use
warn deliberately — the repo bans `console.info`, and warn is what the
current filter passes, so the two halves need not agree on a level.

End-to-end delivery is NOT verified: the unit tests prove the forwarding
logic against a mock, not that the IPC round-trip lands in the file. That
needs a real run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: stop logging absolute paths into shareable diagnostics bundles

`AGENTS.md` forbids absolute paths, usernames and home dirs anywhere,
logs included. Two sites violated it at warn/error, so they were in
bundles today — and this branch is actively asking users to send bundles.
One arrived over Telegram this week.

`postings` logged the full `interactions.json` path four times; the message
already names the file, so most lines lose the path entirely and the rest
log a file name. `extension_bridge` was harder: six browsers share one
manifest filename in different directories, so a bare name would be
ambiguous — it now takes a caller-supplied label instead of deriving
anything from the path.

Swept the whole tree for the class rather than fixing only what was
reported: 90 `.display()` sites and every log/tracing call. No other
production leaks. `std::io::Error` from `fs` does not embed the path in its
Display, and the diagnostics-bundle builder and Sentry already run through
a shared redaction gate — both confirmed rather than assumed.

New architecture rule R15 fails on `.display()` inside a log or tracing
macro, with an empty allowlist. It deliberately ignores `.display()`
elsewhere: a path in an error the user reads about their own file is
legitimate. Four self-tests prove it catches the real multi-line shape
rather than passing vacuously.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: show the user when an export fails instead of nothing at all

We spent two investigations working out what error message the reporter
saw when their PDF would not download. They saw none. Every export trigger
was either a bare try/finally with no catch or a fire-and-forget `void
fn()`, so the backend's perfectly readable "Export blocked: ..." became an
unhandled promise rejection and the button simply did nothing.

That is very likely the literal experience behind "couldn't download it as
pdf".

Three call sites now catch and surface the backend's own message verbatim,
per the pattern #940 set for this path, with a localized fallback only when
the thrown value carries no message. Two more were covered transitively
through the shared modal — including one the original audit missed. The
export modal also stops closing itself on failure, so a retry is possible.

Failures log format, document type and message — never the filename,

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: prove every résumé template's pdf text actually extracts

The leading explanation for the blocked download is `no_extractable_text` —
a critical block that fires when extraction succeeds but returns under 20
characters, the signature of a PDF that renders correctly but whose text
layer is unreadable. It fits the whole evidence set: both document types,
PDF only, DOCX fine (XML, no glyph layer), preview fine (a different
serializer with no text layer at all).

Nothing in the repo could have caught it. One test round-tripped real PDF
text through extraction, covering a single letter/layout/template
combination. The 12-template résumé test asserted only a %PDF header and a
page count, and the two accented-text résumé tests exist to guard a
grapheme-slicing panic and never re-extract. ADR-008 moved subsetting into
the external Typst crates when our renderer was deleted, so no test
verifies that claim at all.

All 12 templates plus the Refined and Banded letter layouts now render and
extract, asserting against the validator's own normalize + 20-char gate so
a pass means the real validator would not have blocked. The fixture uses
Italian grave accents including capitals — the shape the audit found least
tested. Iterating a shared template list means a new template is covered
without remembering to.

Proven to fail: stripping /ToUnicode from the font objects of a real

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: make the renderer log bridge actually reach the log file

The bridge shipped in this PR forwarded console.info through the plugin's
info() wrapper, which sends a `location` derived from the call stack. The Rust
command turns that into the record target `webview:{location}` — and
tauri-plugin-log filters through fern, whose level_for prefix match only walks

dropping the location — the plugin derives it from the 4th stack frame, which
(because this bridge is what calls the plugin) always pointed at log-bridge.ts
rather than the real console caller.

head_commit.message:
fix: bound every http body read, validate probe base urls, and stop reporting failed imports as success (#947)

* fix: bound every http body read through one capped helper in net/http

`read_text_capped` lived in `scraping/http`, so every other subsystem read
response bodies unbounded — a hostile, compromised or merely misconfigured
endpoint could drive the process into OOM. Move it to `net/http`, the
documented centralized HTTP layer (ADR-003), and add `read_bytes_capped`
and `read_json_capped` beside it.

Converted: geocoding, LinkedIn profile import, the six `scrape_url`
resolvers (which hold `get_guarded*` responses — exactly the case the
helper was made `pub(crate)` for), and the LinkedIn client's two binary
reads. Scraping's own `MAX_BYTES` / `FetchOptions::max_bytes` behaviour is
byte-for-byte unchanged; it just calls the moved helper.

The new cap tests force `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` — hyper auto-adds
`Content-Length` for a known-size wiremock body, so a plain response never
exercises the streaming-only guard.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: surface a failed document import instead of toasting success

`documents_import` returns its errors in-band (`{ error, message }`), never
by rejecting, and `use-import-with-ocr` handed every non-`scanned_pdf`
error straight back to the caller. All four consumers got it wrong:
settings and onboarding toasted "Uploaded" unconditionally, and both
`ResumeInputCard` paths guarded on `result.id` with no else, so a failure
produced no feedback at all.

Every one of those call sites already wraps `importFile` in a try/catch, so
the hook now throws — one change, four sites fixed. The post-OCR re-import
was returned unchecked too and gets the same treatment.

Same shape as the LinkedIn import bug in #940: an in-band error nobody
reads, so the success toast lies.

Also: `ResumeStep` took the new document id from the pre-import cached
list rather than the import result, so it could record the wrong default
document — or none at all on a first-ever import.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: persist the embedding format version on cached posting vectors

`get_posting_vector` synthesised `version: EMBEDDING_VECTOR_VERSION` when
rebuilding the space, so `EmbeddingConfig::matches` was structurally
incapable of ever rejecting a row from this table. Freshness rested
entirely on a hand-maintained invariant: every future format bump had to
remember to ship its own eviction migration, or old-format vectors would
read as current under an identical space tag.

Persist the column instead. Existing rows default to 0, so they become a

workflow_runs.display_title: fix: pay off three deferred correctness defects (#946)

head_commit.message:
fix: pay off three deferred correctness defects (#946)

* fix: key cached match scores on the embedding vector version

Cached semantic scores are computed from embeddings, but the cache key
carried provider, model and formula version — not the vector format. A
format change therefore left every stored score a valid hit against vectors
that no longer mean the same thing.

It has been harmless only by coincidence: the format bump in #933 happened to
land with a MATCH_FORMULA_VERSION bump, and that field IS in the key, so the
scores were invalidated by the formula axis rather than by anything reasoning
about vectors. The next format bump without a coincidental formula bump would
have served stale scores as fresh, silently.

The version is now part of the key and of the table's primary key, so a
format change invalidates by construction. Adding an eviction to each future
migration would have been the patch-the-instance answer, and it depends on
whoever writes the next migration remembering — which is the failure this
already survived once by luck.

Every construction site is exhaustive over the struct, so a new one cannot
omit it.

Found alongside: `posting_vectors` has no persisted version column at all and
synthesizes the current one on read, so it cannot self-detect staleness and
still depends on a hand-written eviction per bump. Left alone — that is a
schema change, not this fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: keep a stored cookie's domain scope when rebuilding the jar

Cookies were rebuilt for the reqwest jar as `name=value; Path=...` with no
`Domain`, then added against a URL built from the stored domain with its
leading dot stripped. Per RFC 6265 a cookie with no `Domain` attribute is
host-only, so the leading dot — the very thing marking it as applying to
subdomains — was discarded, and a session captured for `.linkedin.com`
stopped reaching `www.linkedin.com`.

The user-visible effect was that whether a request was authenticated depended
on how the URL happened to be spelled, since both forms pass `detect_platform`.

A stored domain carrying the leading dot now rebuilds with `Domain`, and one
without it stays host-only, matching how it was captured.

Deliberately narrow: `Domain` is only ever the cookie's own stored host, never
anything wider. Widening a session cookie's scope would send a credential to a
host it was never issued for, which is worse than the bug being fixed — so
where the stored shape is ambiguous it stays host-only. `Secure` and
`HttpOnly` were already preserved.

The jar-building loop is extracted so it can be asserted against directly,
`reqwest::Client` not exposing its jar after build. The test that matters is
the safety one — a cookie is never attached to an unrelated host — and it was
confirmed load-bearing by temporarily broadening the code and watching it fail.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: gate gemini's top_p on the same rule that already gates temperature

Google deprecated temperature, top_p and top_k together for Gemini 3.x —
ignored today, documented as a future 400. `temperature` got a per-model gate
when the reasoning-effort work landed; `topP` was left behind in the same
commit, so two halves of one API rule disagreed about the same models.

Both now run through a single `gemini_omits_sampling_params` predicate over
the existing v3 boundary, so a future model cannot be gated for one parameter
and not the other. Sharing the rule is the fix; sharing it is also what was
missing when this defect was created.

`topP` is omitted on v3+ even when explicitly set, deliberately unlike
temperature's explicit-always-wins carve-out. Temperature is a user dial, so
an explicit value expresses intent worth honouring. `topP` here is set by our
own anti-detection code, so there is no user intent to preserve and nothing
worth risking a future 400 for. The reasoning is in the doc comments, since a
reader would otherwise "correct" the asymmetry.

Verified against Google's current docs rather than inherited from the earlier
review: both the Gemini 3.x parameter guidance and the sampling-deprecation
note group all three parameters identically, and apply to the classic
GenerateContent API rather than only the newer surface. `top_k` is never sent
anywhere in this adapter, so it needs no gate today.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat: add a tech radar that fails the build when an entry goes stale (#941)

* feat: add a tech radar that fails the build when an entry goes stale

A public /tech-radar page: what this project adopts, trials, assesses and
holds, with the reasoning, linked to the ADR where one genuinely covers that
choice.

The interesting problem is not the drawing, it is that a radar is a curated
judgement artifact — the same shape as the hardcoded model lists this repo
just spent two PRs deleting because they rot silently. Deriving it from the
manifests would remove the judgement that makes a radar worth reading, so
entries stay curated and staleness is made to fail loudly instead: every
entry carries a lastReviewed date, and check:tech-radar fails when an entry
names a dependency no longer present in any package.json or Cargo.toml.

Note the deliberate asymmetry with the check rejected for model lists. That
one would have fired on RATES rows that are retained on purpose so historical
spend still prices correctly. A radar entry naming a removed dependency has
no such justification. Entries that are not dependencies at all — techniques,
hosted services, and the deliberately-not-adopted — declare a subjectKind and
are exempt, because a check that cries wolf gets ignored, which is precisely
why the model-list version was dropped.

Quadrants are named for this project's real shape rather than Thoughtworks'
generic set, which would have left two of four nearly empty.

Rendered as hand-written inline SVG: the landing site has three runtime
dependencies and a radar is polar-to-cartesian arcs and dots, so d3 would
have cost more than it saved. Rings are encoded by shape as well as colour,
every blip is a focusable anchor, and the full data is always present as a
text list — the SVG is decoration over it, not the only copy. The a11y gate
caught a real contrast failure during development; the fix uses the token
file's own vetted accent.

The route is in the sitemap and linked from the footers. #934 exists because
/how-it-works had no inbound links and was never indexed; a brand-new route
is exactly where that repeats.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: close the gaps review found in the radar's own staleness argument

Two of these landed on the argument this feature is built on.

The check guarded against parsing zero entries — total drift — but nothing
caught losing some. Its brace walk tracked ' and " and not backticks or
comments, so one apostrophe inside a template-literal rationale ran past the
closing brace and swallowed the following entry. It would have printed OK
while verifying 38 of 40. The walker now handles both, and a count assertion
requires the raw id: lines inside the array to equal the parsed entries, so a
partial drop cannot pass quietly.

The published accessibility statement claimed zero violations across twelve
enumerated routes. The a11y gate discovers routes by globbing built HTML, so
this page silently made it thirteen — a public conformance claim staled by a
change whose whole argument is that staleness should fail loudly. Corrected in
both places that carried the count, and the route is in llms.txt now too.

The check also verified package names while the page published versions, so
upgrading React to 20 would leave the manifest matching and the page claiming
19. Entry names carry a bare major, checked against the manifest's declared
range; unparseable ranges are skipped rather than failed, since a check that
misfires is worse than none. Ids are now asserted unique — id is a React key,
a DOM anchor and the layout map key at once — and lastReviewed must be a real
date, being the field the whole design rests on.

The overlap work found something better than the reported issue. The closest
pair in the real data was not two blips in one cell but two in adjacent
quadrants at the same ring, 6.85 units apart — a case no single-cell test
could reach. Retuned the wedge padding and radius fractions, and the test now
asserts minimum pairwise separation rather than mere distinctness.

Worth recording: 28 units is not achievable at ten entries in the Adopt band
under any packing found, so the layout targets the real 24px WCAG floor, which
it now clears with margin. The comment that asserted 2.5.8 unconditionally
said so at full width only; it no longer overclaims.
